content: The biceps is a muscle found in two pairs within the human body, one on the right side and one on the left. The term biceps originates from the Latin adjective meaning two-headed. These muscles are named as such because each of them has two points of origin, or insertions, at their upper end. In common usage, the term biceps typically refers to the biceps brachii, which is the prominent muscle located on the inner side of each upper arm. This muscle is often associated with physical strength due to its ability to flex in a highly visible manner. Less commonly, the term biceps can also refer to the biceps femoris, which is one of the hamstring muscles located on the underside of each thigh. It is important to note that biceps is the correct singular form of the term. However, the muscle is frequently and incorrectly referred to as a bicep.
